name: Education
one_liner: Schools, universities, and education companies delivering learning, a sector shaped by public funding, enrollment demographics, and a slow-to-change cost base.
how_it_makes_money: Universities earn tuition, government funding, research grants, and endowment returns, while K-12 is mostly funded by state and local taxes. Education companies sell courseware, learning platforms, test prep, and online programs through institutional licenses, subscriptions, or revenue-share partnerships.
revenue_formula: Tuition revenue = enrolled students × sticker price × (1 − discount rate)
EdTech revenue = institutions or users × seats × price per seat
cost_structure: Faculty and staff compensation: typically the largest cost, often over half of spending
Student financial aid: institutional scholarships that offset tuition
Technology and content development for online and EdTech providers
margins: Most universities and schools are nonprofit or public and aim to run near break-even, while for-profit education and EdTech firms range from losses to roughly 15-25% operating margins. Enrollment scale, discount rates, and delivery mix drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Enrollment
key_metrics.what: Number of students; the main revenue driver and sensitive to demographics.

key_metrics.name: Tuition discount rate
key_metrics.what: Share of sticker price given back as aid; rising rates erode net revenue.

key_metrics.name: Yield
key_metrics.what: Share of admitted students who enroll; indicates brand strength and pricing power.

key_metrics.name: Retention and graduation rates
key_metrics.what: Share of students persisting and completing; affects revenue, rankings, and funding.

key_metrics.name: Cost per student
key_metrics.what: Spending per enrolled student; a key efficiency benchmark.

key_metrics.name: Student outcomes
key_metrics.what: Job placement and earnings after completion; increasingly used to judge ROI.

trends: Shrinking college-age population in the US pressuring smaller private colleges and leading to closures and mergers
Generative AI changing how students learn and how institutions assess work
Growth of skills-based credentials, bootcamps, and employer-sponsored learning
Scrutiny of higher-education ROI and student debt
Policy shifts in federal education funding, research grants, and international student visas
Consolidation in online program management and EdTech after the pandemic boom

case_angles.question: A private university faces declining enrollment and a budget deficit; what should it do?
Should a university launch a fully online degree program?
How should an EdTech company respond to free AI tutoring tools?
A state wants to improve its high-school graduation rates; how should it allocate funding?

interview_hooks: Is the four-year degree still worth the cost for most students?
Will AI tutors democratize education or widen gaps?
Should struggling colleges merge, close, or reinvent themselves?
